text:
Jamie (ops): noticing elevated 5xx from edge -> backend in us-west-2, ELB & route53 spikes. customers reporting timeouts :exclamation:
SRE Pager: paging oncall for us-west-2 network anomalies. sev2.
Oncall Bot: @oncall-sre pager triggered (policy: region-networking) — escalation in progress.
Maria K: I'm on it, pulling ELB metrics and NLB target health now.
Raj P: I see route53 healthchecks showing increased latency and some NXDOMAINs for internal cname lookups.
Ana (support): getting customer reports: "api.redwood.ai" 503 for several accounts across us-west.
Jamie (ops): customers hit seems ~5% of production traffic, concentrated in us-west AZB/C.
Maria K: ELB target group shows high 502/504 from a subset of instances, but instance-level CPU/memory normal.
Raj P: check ENI stats — rx/tx errors on a few ENIs in azb. Could be NIC driver/reprovisioning flapping.
inc-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0423 - us-west-2 reachability - Sev2. Assigned to oncall-sre.
SRE Pager: handoff to Maria K for mitigation. Maria, prefer cold-restart of affected instances or failover to healthy AZ?
Maria K: start controlled failover: mark unhealthy targets for azb/nlba, drain connections, shift traffic to azc & azd.
DevEx Tom: adding a temporary routing policy in Route53 to prefer eu-west for critical APIs as a safety valve (low TTL).
Jamie (ops): good. lower Route53 TTL to 30s for apex and api record to speed any client failover.
Maria K: runbook step: set ELB connection draining to 45s, deregister targets in AZB, monitor latency.
Maria K: command: ```aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:... --targets Id=i-0abc123 --region us-west-2```
Raj P: running ENI diagnostics: ```sudo ethtool -S eth0 | grep -E "rx_errors|tx_errors"``` on node i-0abc123 shows rx_errors spike.
Ana (support): posted interim update to status.redwood.ai: "Partial API errors in us-west-2, mitigation in progress" :white_check_mark: customers advised to retry.
SRE Pager: acceptance criteria: error rate < 1% on api route and ELB unhealthy count back to baseline.
Maria K: after draining, error rate dropped from 6.2% -> 1.8% in 4 minutes. still above SLO. continuing drain on remaining suspects.
Oncall Bot: automatic fallback triggered for 2 noncritical routes to small-model-variant in other region.
Raj P: suspect networking link issue inside AZB — opening AWS support case: case-id 1234567890. Provided packet captures and ENI IDs.
Jamie (ops): if AWS confirms local AZ fabric issue we should plan permanent traffic shift and capacity rebalancing.
DevEx Tom: posting an ops note to #postmortems with initial timeline and commands we ran.
Maria K: after shifting majority of traffic, error rate now 0.4% and p95 latency back to normal. marking incident as mitigated.
SRE Pager: starting 30m monitoring window before closing. please continue to collect diagnostic artifacts.
Ana (support): customers updated with ETA for fully resolved and pointer to SR with support team. one enterprise customer escalated to account team.
inc-bot: Incident status: Mitigated -> Monitoring.
Raj P: AWS replied: "We observed transient NIC firmware-induced packet drops confined to us-west-2a/b; replacement scheduled for impacted hosts."
Maria K: saved tcpdump snapshots, elb logs, and instance syslogs to s3://redwood-incident-archive/INC-2026-0423/ for postmortem.```
SRE Pager: handoff to oncall-sre-2 for continued watch. @oncall-sre-2 please ack.
DevEx Tom: note for postmortem: consider adding automated route53 weighted failover playbook and a runbook item to preemptively lower TTL during suspected AZ fabric issues.
Jamie (ops): thanks everyone. quick retro after we close — want to capture timelines and customer impact matrix. :thumbsup:
Oncall Bot: @oncall-sre-2 acknowledged handoff.
Ana (support): creating follow-up tickets for all affected customers with incident summary and remediation.
inc-bot: Incident INC-2026-0423 moved to Resolved (after monitoring) at 1710001850.
